text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 2.2% today to $393.26, extending a sharp 8% decline over the past week. The timing aligns with a pullback in oil prices: U.S. crude is down to $89.62 per barrel today after the stock peaked at $414.65 on November 13th when oil was trading higher. Refiners like Marathon profit most when the gap between crude input costs and refined product prices widens, so when crude softens without a matching drop in gasoline and diesel prices, margins compress.

The broader concern for refiners right now is that demand signals are mixed. Heating oil is up 59% year-over-year, which could suggest strong winter demand, but retailers are being cautious on holiday inventory as shipping costs rise—a potential headwind for overall fuel consumption. Refineries are already running at 95.2% capacity with ample oil in storage (693.95 million barrels), leaving little room to ramp up production if demand disappoints.
